# Reverting a seal puts the old content back, merged onto what HEAD holds now:
# later edits stay, conflicting ones leave markers to resolve by hand.

env GIT_EDITOR=true
sesam-repo admin v1.txt v2.txt v3.txt v4.txt t1.txt t2.txt resolved.txt
exec sesam hook install

cp $TMPDIR/v1.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/t1.txt t
exec sesam add s t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s and t'

cp $TMPDIR/v2.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'change s'

cp $TMPDIR/t2.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'change t'

# The drivers would merge the log backwards for an older commit. The log driver
# refuses, which aborts the whole revert before any secret was touched.
! exec git revert --no-edit HEAD~1
stderr 'would remove entries from the append-only audit log'
stderr 'run .sesam revert <commit>. instead'
exec git status --porcelain
! stdout .
cmp s $TMPDIR/v2.txt

# t changed since, but not in the reverted commit: it is left alone.
exec sesam revert HEAD~1
stdout '^~ content of s$'
! stdout 'content of t'
exec git revert --continue
cmp s $TMPDIR/v1.txt
cmp t $TMPDIR/t2.txt
exec sesam status
! stdout 'not in sync|stale|diverged'
exec sesam verify --all
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
! stderr 'not a prefix'

# A clean checkout reveals the reverted content.
rm s
exec sesam reveal
cmp s $TMPDIR/v1.txt

# Now one that conflicts: s changed on the same line after the reverted commit.
cp $TMPDIR/v4.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'change s again'
cp $TMPDIR/v3.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'and again'

exec sesam revert HEAD~1
stdout '^! content of s \(1 conflict\)$'
stderr 'resolve the conflict markers in s, then run .sesam seal s. and .git add .sesam.'
grep '^<<<<<<<' s

# The hook refuses to commit markers.
! exec git revert --continue
stderr 'unresolved conflicts'

cp $TMPDIR/resolved.txt s
exec sesam seal s
exec git add .sesam
exec git revert --continue
cmp s $TMPDIR/resolved.txt
exec sesam verify --all
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
! stderr 'not a prefix'

-- v1.txt --
user=alice
password=one
-- v2.txt --
user=alice
password=two
-- v3.txt --
user=alice
password=three
-- v4.txt --
user=alice
password=four
-- t1.txt --
token=a
-- t2.txt --
token=b
-- resolved.txt --
user=alice
password=resolved
